sources.citation: Gell, Alfred. 1975 [Routledge eBook reissue 2020, ISBN 9781000320947]. Metamorphosis of the Cassowaries: Umeda Society, Language and Ritual. LSE Monographs on Social Anthropology 51. London: Athlone Press / Abingdon: Routledge. Publisher preview PDF, 39 pp. (front matter, contents, ch. 1 'The Umeda Setting' and ch. 2 'The Social Structure of Umeda Village' to p. 28).
sources.note: Nothing on word stress or tone as a system. The only prosodic content in the 39 preview pages is incidental: Umeda speakers' pronunciations of the five village names are given with stress marks ('umda with first-syllable stress; 'puda, sa'wada [= Sowanda], 'waina, wa'yala). Ch. 3 'Language and Symbolism' (pp. 119 ff.), where any orthographic or phonological note would sit, is not in the preview; the 1973 thesis version of that material (held by the project) has no stress/tone statement either.

sources.note: Nothing. The Waina (Sowanda) chapter is a desk compilation: names, dialects (Waina, Punda-Umeda), population, Loving & Bass 1964 and Seiler 1985 lexicostatistic percentages, a pronoun comparison table and bibliographic notes ('For Waina, Seiler 1985 contains short wordlists and there is unpublished Waina data in Laycock nd'). The only prosody words in the document are in bibliography titles for Ok-family and Karkar-Yuri languages (Price 1981/1982 Karkar stress, Steinkraus Tifal tone, Smith & Weston Mianmin tonemes); section 7.4 'Phonology and morphology' concerns Mountain Ok only.

sources.citation: Seiler, Walter. 1985. Imonda, a Papuan language. Pacific Linguistics B-93. Canberra: ANU. Sec. 1.1.2 (p. 3), 1.2 (p. 4), Appendix A 'Imonda and related languages' (pp. 210-218).
sources.note: Nothing for Sowanda. Appendix A gives a comparative wordlist (Imonda, Daonda, Waris, Simog, Sowanda, Punda) with an orthography note (A.1.1: near-phonemic spelling, prenasalisation not marked; Punda voiced stops not prenasalised), then number marking, nominaliser and case. The only stress statement in the book (p. 10, 'stress being approximately equal on all syllables') is about Imonda. p. 4: previous work on Waris languages = wordlists only; 'Ethnographic data on the Waina area and some scattered words are to be found in Gell (1975)'.

sources.citation: Seiler, Walter. 1984. The main structures of Imonda: a Papuan language. PhD thesis, Australian National University. xi+372 leaves. (Appendix A 'Imonda and related languages': comparative wordlist and morphology of Imonda, Daonda, Waris, Simog, Sowanda, Punda.)
sources.note: Only prosodic statement (thesis p. 20 = 1985:10) concerns Imonda: 'As far as suprasegmentals are concerned, tone and stress have no contrastive function, stress being approximately equal on all syllables.' Appendix A.1.1 'Observations' on the Sowanda/Punda/Waris/Daonda/Simog lists covers only segmental orthography (near-phonemic spelling; secondary labialisation, prenasalisation of voiced stops and offglides not marked; Punda voiced stops not prenasalised). No stress or tone remark for Sowanda; wordlist carries no stress marks.
